The Babylon Fire, burning 25 miles southwest of Monicello, was last mapped at 70,735 acres and 0% containment. The fire, burning 25 miles southwest of Monicello, was last mapped at 70,735 acres and 0% containment.
On Tuesday, it was mapped at 48,000 acres. Roads closed as firefighters battle Babylon Fire amid dangerous weather conditionsFire crews continued to work on the southern portion of the fire perimeter on Tuesday, "constructing and improving the heel of the fire using direct extinguishment strategies," according to the US Forest Service Manti-La Sal National Forest.
"Direct extinguishment strategy allows firefighters to secure the perimeter while constructing fireline directly along the fire’s edge," the Forest Service continued. "This suppression strategy, also known as 'keeping one foot in the black' provide a safe anchor point by removing fuel directly along the fire’s edge during suppression efforts. " Firefighters worked on Wednesday to use areas of reduced vegetation to their advantage and mitigate the fire's spread on the western perimeter.
"However, with wind gusts up to 20 mph and single-digit relative humidity forecast across the fire area, fire activity is expected to increase in the Peavine and Dark Canyon drainages," the Forest Service said. A Red Flag Warning was in effect until 8 p.m. on Wednesday for gusty winds, low relative humidity, and dry fuels.
Smoke was expected to increase significantly overnight as the fire grows eastward, "with air quality potentially reaching very unhealthy or hazardous levels," the Forest Service said.
